PARTIAL: STATUS: partial (audit complete; in_review report refused because worktree is dirty with pre-existing/unrelated changes)
CHANGES: none (read-only audit)
BUILD/TYPECHECK/TESTS: not run; read-only audit used rg/sed/nl only.
FINDINGS:
1. High: backend emits structured bad_mode but CLI has no renderer, so common mode mistakes leak raw RPC. Backend serializes PlanError::BadMode as {type:"bad_mode"} at src-tauri/src/service/plan/mod.rs:209; plan.mode.set creates it on invalid mode at src-tauri/src/socket/server/plan_mode.rs:21-28, and plan.update can also surface it via update_plan after cli/src/cmd/plan.rs:405-422. cli/src/cmd/plan_errors.rs:35-85 does not match bad_mode, so fallback at cli/src/cmd/plan_errors.rs:13-17 prints `RPC error -32603: invalid plan mode`. Recommended message: `✗ invalid plan mode. valid modes: planning|approved|execution|complete. fix: codeterm plan mode <plan_id> --set approved` or for update `codeterm plan update <plan_id> --mode approved`. Tests: add render_plan_error bad_mode unit test in cli/src/cmd/plan/tests.rs and a command-level test/stub asserting `codeterm plan mode pl --set garbage` does not include `RPC error`.
2. High: backend emits structured bad_priority but CLI has no renderer, so task add/update/record priority failures leak raw RPC. Backend serializes PlanError::BadPriority at src-tauri/src/service/plan/mod.rs:210; task add maps invalid priority at src-tauri/src/socket/server/plan.rs:722-727, and parsing helpers also map it in src-tauri/src/service/plan/mutations.rs:109-112 and src-tauri/src/service/plan/readback.rs:52-54. cli/src/cmd/plan_errors.rs:35-85 lacks bad_priority. Recommended message: `✗ invalid task priority. valid priorities: low|normal|high|urgent` plus the exact retry command, e.g. `codeterm plan task update <plan_id> <task_id> --priority normal`. Tests: add renderer unit test and a plan task add/update CLI error test that asserts no raw RPC.
3. High: `not_found` renderer is overconfident and wrong for spec/section/handoff/loop/heartbeat contexts. The backend uses the single PlanError::NotFound type for many resources (serialized at src-tauri/src/service/plan/mod.rs:193), but cli/src/cmd/plan_errors.rs:41-43 always says `no plan <id> was found` and suggests `codeterm plan list --active`. Examples: `codeterm spec show missing` calls call_plan_rpc with only spec_id at cli/src/cmd/spec.rs:124-129, while spec lookup returns NotFound at src-tauri/src/service/plan/spec.rs:97-107; missing spec section also returns NotFound at src-tauri/src/service/plan/section_queries.rs:27-36. `codeterm plan loop stop/status/advance missing` returns NotFound from src-tauri/src/service/plan/loop_mutations.rs:79-125 but CLI will mention a plan. `codeterm orchestrator heartbeat show` without a resolvable active plan returns NotFound at src-tauri/src/service/plan/heartbeat.rs:172-202 and will print `no plan <id>`. Recommended shape: infer from params: spec_id -> `no spec ...; fix: codeterm spec list --active`; section_id -> `no section ...; fix: codeterm plan/spec section show/list ...`; loop_id -> `no loop ...; fix: codeterm plan get <plan_id> or codeterm plan loop status <loop_id>`; heartbeat with no plan_id -> `no active plan owned by this orchestrator pane/session; fix: pass --plan <plan_id> or run codeterm plan list --active`. Tests: add render_plan_error not_found cases with spec_id, section_id, loop_id, and heartbeat params.
4. Medium: `bad_status` renderer is task-specific but backend also uses it for plan status. Backend serializes BadStatus at src-tauri/src/service/plan/mod.rs:208; plan.update maps invalid PlanStatus at src-tauri/src/socket/server/plan.rs:405-412. CLI renderer at cli/src/cmd/plan_errors.rs:37-40 says `invalid task status`, lists task statuses, and suggests `codeterm plan task update ...`, which is wrong for `codeterm plan update <plan_id> --status garbage`. Recommended shape: if params include task_id use current task guidance; otherwise say `invalid plan status. valid statuses: active|archived|done|cancelled` and suggest `codeterm plan update <plan_id> --status active`. Tests: split bad_status renderer tests for task_id and plan-only params.
5. Medium: structured io errors still fall back to raw RPC, including actionable handoff errors. Backend serializes PlanError::Io with {type:"io", message} at src-tauri/src/service/plan/mod.rs:238, but cli/src/cmd/plan_errors.rs:35-85 has no io branch. Some Io is truly internal, but user-actionable cases exist: handoff reseed mode/source/session/active-pending errors at src-tauri/src/service/plan/handoff.rs:428-443 and 464-467. Today these become `RPC error -32603: mode must be new or compact` or `handoff reseed already pending...`. Recommended shape: for handoff-ish messages, prefix with product context and command, e.g. `✗ cannot reseed handoff: a reseed is already pending for pane <pane>. fix: rerun with codeterm orchestrator handoff --plan <plan_id> --pane <pane> --reseed --force, or wait for the pending reseed to finish.` Generic io renderer should avoid the RPC prefix: `✗ planner write/read failed: <message>` and include `do not retry blindly` only for write/read ambiguity. Tests: renderer unit tests for io generic and handoff pending/mode messages.
6. Medium: orchestrator handoff has two raw non-plan RPC bypasses. `status` calls `client.call("agent.reports", ...)` directly at cli/src/cmd/orchestrator.rs:111-117 before the rendered `plan.state` call; if this ever errors it will use SocketCallError Display (`RPC error ...`) rather than a workflow message. `handoff --reseed` reads pane metadata through `client.call("pane.list", None)` at cli/src/cmd/orchestrator.rs:429-442; transport/RPC failures also bypass render_plan_call_error, and local errors say `pane <id> not found` / `has no source session id` without suggested commands. Recommended shape: wrap these as orchestrator-specific messages: `✗ cannot read orchestrator reports for pane <pane>; fix: codeterm pane list` and `✗ cannot reseed: pane <pane> is not an agent pane or has no session; fix: codeterm pane list --agents and pass --pane <agent-pane>`. Tests: unit-test pane_session_id error rendering if extracted, and add a mocked SocketClient path or lower-level renderer test for orchestrator non-plan RPC errors.
7. Low/Medium: fallback still intentionally exposes raw RPC for structured-but-unknown plan errors. cli/src/cmd/plan_errors.rs:13-17 prints `RPC error code: message` whenever data.type is unknown or unhandled. That is exactly why newly added PlanError variants leak until CLI is updated. Recommended guard: if `rpc.data.type` exists but no renderer matches, print `planner error: <message>` plus `unhandled structured type: <type>` only in JSON/debug mode, or add a CI/unit test asserting every PlanError::to_json type in src-tauri/src/service/plan/mod.rs has a renderer. Tests: snapshot/list test covering all current types: not_found, element_not_found, task_not_found, open_subtasks, transition_denied, undeclared_kind, budget_exhausted, bad_status, bad_mode, bad_priority, task_creation_requires_approval, heartbeat_requires_execution, write_pending, readback_mismatch, io.
KNOWN ISSUE CHECK: The transition_denied draft covers the reported `codeterm plan record ... --status done` on in_review. Record goes through call_plan_rpc("plan.batch") at cli/src/cmd/plan_record.rs:159-167, and transition_denied is rendered at cli/src/cmd/plan_errors.rs:55 and cli/src/cmd/plan_errors.rs:88-104 with the specific in_review->done wording. Existing test cli/src/cmd/plan/tests.rs:64-79 asserts the intended close/bounce guidance.
FOLLOWUP: Add missing renderers first (bad_mode, bad_priority, context-aware not_found/bad_status, io), then wrap orchestrator non-plan RPCs. The requested --status in_review report was attempted and refused by CodeTerm due dirty files: .codeterm plan files, cli/src/cmd/plan/tests.rs, cli/src/cmd/plan_errors.rs, src-tauri/src/service/hierarchy/plan_reminder_nudge.rs, src-tauri/src/service/plan/worker_charter.rs. No source files were modified by this audit.

Accepted. Read-only audit found missing/weak planner CLI error renderers: bad_mode, bad_priority, context-aware not_found and bad_status, io, orchestrator handoff/status non-plan RPC bypasses, plus a guard against unknown structured PlanError types falling back to raw RPC. Known transition_denied issue is covered by the current patch.
